Noelle (AE): Beth from ACME sent back their vendor risk review. primary concerns: can we do BYOK for hosted, how do we prove keys are HSM-backed, and what's the exact language we can put in the CAIQ.
Ravi (SecEng): quick reply: yes to BYOK. we support two hosted BYOK modes: 1) KMS integration (cloud provider KMS, reference by ARN) where keys never leave customer KMS, and 2) wrapped-key import for Private where customer supplies a wrapped KEK; Redwood never receives unwrapped KEK.
Lina (Solutions): add-on: for Dedicated/Private we can also point to customer KMIP endpoint for on-prem HSMs. supported HSMs in POC: AWS CloudHSM, Thales nShield, Gemalto/Thales HSMs with KMIP.
Marcus (Infra): HSM attestation: we can provide FIPS certs and an attestation PDF that includes the HSM vendor, module ID, cert chain, and a signed statement of key generation location. we publish this to a secure link prior to demos.
Beth (ACME): one requirement: we need to ensure Redwood does not have the ability to decrypt customer data unless we explicitly opt-in with dual-approval. can you confirm?
Ravi (SecEng): confirmed. default posture: Redwood services do not have access to plaintext customer data keys. for Redwood-managed KMS cases we provide documented emergency access procedures only under contract with dual-approval and audit trail. BYOK customers retain enforcement of rotation and revocation via their KMS.
Noelle (AE): legal wants a short contract blurb they can paste.
Ravi (SecEng): suggested language: "Redwood encrypts customer data at rest using AES-256-GCM with an envelope-key architecture. Customers may provide and manage wrapping keys via supported KMS integrations (BYOK) or KMIP HSM endpoints; HSM-backed keys meet applicable FIPS validations. Redwood does not export customer key material in plaintext and access to key material is restricted, logged, and subject to dual-approval emergency procedures where applicable."
Lina (Solutions): they also asked for a 3-step POC to validate non-escrow and attestation. my checklist: 1) spin up Dedicated POC and configure customer KMS key ARN or KMIP endpoint, 2) ingest sample data and show ciphertext + KMS describe-key output, 3) rotate wrapping key in customer KMS and demonstrate application continuity and show uploaded attestation PDF.
Marcus (Infra): implementation note for POC: we will show live KMS describe-key, CloudHSM key id, and audit log events (key:encrypt, key:decrypt) streamed to a temporary S3 bucket. will not place any unwrapped key material in logs.
Beth (ACME): timeline: can you upload attestation and sample describe-key outputs before our call on Thursday?
Marcus (Infra): yes, ETA Wed evening. I'll upload signed attestation to secure storage and post link.
AttestBot: attestation-upload: https://redwood-secure.s3/attestations/acme-2026-hsm-attest.pdf (expires in 7d) :lock: :white_check_mark:
Noelle (AE): great — I'll paste Ravi's blurb + Lina's POC checklist into the CAIQ responses and send to ACME legal. ping here if we need to change the wording to be more specific to their regs. :thumbsup:
